title: Early Life Exposure to Manure-Fertilized Soil Shapes the Gut Antibiotic Resistome.
ehr_evidence: Soil samples were collected from two distinct locations: red soil (RS, classified as Ultisols) from Xinhui District, Jiangmen City, Guangdong Province and black soil (BS, classified as Mollisols) from Hailun City, Suihua, Heilongjiang Province.
summary: Experimental study investigating how early life exposure to manure-fertilized soil alters the gut antibiotic resistome and microbiome composition in mice.
key_findings: Manured red soil ARG abundance was 0.63 ± 0.03 copies/cell, a 10.5% increase over unfertilized soil (0.57 ± 0.005 copies/cell, P < 0.05).
Manured black soil ARG abundance was 0.45 ± 0.02 copies/cell, a 12.5% increase over unfertilized soil (0.40 ± 0.02 copies/cell, P < 0.05).
Mouse gut ARG abundance in the manured red soil group was 3.34 ± 0.34 copies/cell, a 48.4% increase over the control group (2.25 ± 0.37 copies/cell).
Mouse gut ARG abundance in the manured black soil group was 3.89 ± 0.62 copies/cell, a 109% increase over the control group (1.86 ± 0.54 copies/cell).
Tetracycline resistance genes comprised 84.9% of gut ARGs, with tet(Q) constituting 90% of tetracycline ARGs.
MGE abundance was significantly higher in manured groups (Manured RS: 34.21 ± 2.47 copies/cell, 12.5% increase; Manured BS: 36.07 ± 4.43 copies/cell, 19.8% increase).
Virulence factor abundance was elevated in manured groups (Manured RS: 12.78 ± 1.09 copies/cell, 8.7% increase; Manured BS: 11.61 ± 0.61 copies/cell, 13.44% increase).
captured_features: Gut microbiome composition (phylum and family level)
data_source_type: metagenomic sequencing of soil and fecal samples
population: BALB/c mice (pregnant dams and offspring from birth to 8 weeks)
limitations: animal model (mice) limits direct human translatability
small sample size per group (n=3 pregnant mice)
controlled laboratory conditions may not reflect real-world agricultural environments
cross-sectional sampling at a single timepoint (8 weeks)
data_availability_statement: The raw metagenomic sequence data are publicly available under the accession number PRJNA1206751.
